cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Credit for the Impossible
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I believed the cupboard before it learned to speak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. One quick acknowledgment, then I'll respect its wishes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says you talk too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An informed opinion formed over years of my support.

mechanism: A controls public introduction order to obtain acknowledgment of believing in the talking cupboard before others did.
confusable: Unlike praising the cupboard or defending A's verbosity, the dialogue must seek explicit credit for earlier acceptance.
comparison: A public introduction and cupboard's self-introduction compete for precedence, distinct from staircase date and volume.
seedUse: Use only the canonical talking-cupboard and silence seed as recorded context; write a different introduction-order tactic, not the staged single candidate's written-credit tactic.
